title: Discovery recap — trial charter options & grading approach
text:
Discovery recap — trial charter options & grading approach

['From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@findwell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap — trial charter options & grading approach

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap from our side and two suggested routes for the trial so we can pick the right approach for your engineering & compliance constraints.

Highlights from the call:
- Primary goal: reduce manual triage time for clinical content extraction by ~60% on the 3 MVP flows you demoed.
- Hard constraints: PII must never leave your VPC; model must pass policy-filtering on 3 sample documents.
- Success bar is team-aligned: accuracy on entity extraction + endpoint latency under 350ms median.

Two trial approaches we recommend (high level):
1) Shadow evaluation (online):
   - Run Redwood in shadow mode alongside your production pipeline for 10 business days.
   - Measure real traffic results (latency, token cost, entity F1) and compare to baseline.
   - Pros: most realistic; surfaces integration quirks.
   - Cons: requires a small routing change and technical sign-off from your SREs.

2) Offline/Rerun evaluation (batch):
   - Redwood runs against your anonymized sample set (we process within your VPC).
   - Use an agreed grading rubric to score extractions + hallucination checks.
   - Pros: faster to start, minimal runtime impact.
   - Cons: may miss runtime-specific latency/edge cases.

Attached: a draft trial charter and a small sample dataset (anonymized) we discussed — see "Findwell_trial_charter_v1.pdf" and "Findwell_MVP_data_sample.csv". Also attached a starter scoring rubric.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm which route you prefer (Shadow vs Offline) by EOD Wed so we can lock scheduler & SRE time.
- If Shadow: we’ll schedule a 60-minute runbook review with your SREs and provide a short rollback plan.
- If Offline: we’ll sign an NDA addendum and ingest the sample within 48 hours of receipt.

Owners: Ben (sales) to coordinate schedule; Marissa (solutions) to own the trial charter; Karthik (success) to own scoring and dashboards.

Thanks — happy to hop back on a quick call tomorrow if you want to walk the options live.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

', 'From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@findwell.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Findwell Tech Ops <tech@findwell.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — trial charter options & grading approach

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. A few clarifications before we pick a path:

1) Shadow concerns: our security team is wary about any model inference leaving our VPC. You mentioned Redwood supports private deployments — would shadow run inside our VPC or would we need a staging hop?
2) Scoring rubric: can you add a simple false-positive penalty so that precision is weighted more heavily for certain clinical entity types?
3) Timeline: if we opt for offline, how long between data handoff and first results?

If we get answers to those 3 points today, I can confirm which route we prefer. We are leaning toward Offline for speed, but we need the rubric tweak and a clear SLA on data handling.

Best,
Jane
Director, Product — Findwell Health

', 'From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@findwell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — trial charter options & grading approach

Hi Jane — great questions. Answers below and an updated proposal attached.

1) Shadow security: Redwood supports both private (VPC) shadow and hosted shadow. For your security posture we recommend Private Shadow: Redwood controller runs in your VPC (no egress), inference happens on instances you control or in a peered account. I’ve added the VPC deployment checklist to the charter (see attachment).

2) Scoring rubric: yes — we can make precision-heavy weighting for clinical-critical entity classes. Suggested quick rubric fields (included in redwood-grading-rubric.xlsx):
   - Entity F1 (40%)
   - Clinical-critical precision (weighted precision for diagnosis/medication) (40%)
   - Hallucination / false-insertions penalty (-10% per high-risk incident)
   - Latency SLO compliance (10%)

   Example grading buckets: Excellent > 85, Acceptable 70-85, Rework < 70.

3) Offline timeline: once we receive the anonymized sample and an executed addendum, first pass results typically in 48–72 hours (small sets) and 5 business days for larger runs (tens of thousands of docs).

Next steps I propose (concrete):
- You: confirm Offline vs Private Shadow by EOD Wednesday (2027-04-14).
- If Offline: upload the anonymized sample to the shared drive link and sign the addendum in the attached charter. We’ll queue the run and deliver initial scorecards within 72 hours.
- If Private Shadow: schedule SRE runbook meeting — suggest Thu 4/15 or Fri 4/16 (30–60 min).

I’ve also attached the updated trial charter (Findwell_trial_charter_v1.pdf) with a short section on data handling, ownership, and rollback.

Attachments referenced: Findwell_trial_charter_v1.pdf; Findwell_MVP_data_sample.csv; redwood-grading-rubric.xlsx

Happy to iterate on the rubric if you want the weights tuned further.

—
Ben

', 'From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Findwell — recommended approach before we lock schedule

Quick internal note to align before we go final with Jane.

Recommendation summary:
- Lean Offline initially (fastest path to measurable quality; lower operational friction).
- Include precision-heavy weighting for diagnosis/medication entities per Ben’s rubric.
- Add a short safety gate: if hallucination incidents > 2 in initial batch, pause and propose focused model tuning.
- Karthik: please prep a live dashboard template (per-entity precision/recall, hallucination count, median latency) so we can deliver a clean scorecard.
- Ben: confirm addendum + upload instructions in the charter; ask Jane for a sample upload window.

Procurement note: I’ll loop in Finance if they ask for trial terms — better to pre-authorize the small compute allowance we mentioned on the call (covers the offline run).

Will wait for Jane’s confirmation then finalize calendar invites.

—
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
']
